However, if harm is caused in good faith for the benefit of such a person, it is not considered an offence (Section 27).
summary_answer: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, a person of unsound mind is not held liable for an act if they are incapable of understanding the nature of the act or that it is wrong (Section 22). However, if harm is caused in good faith for the benefit of such a person, it is not considered an offence (Section 27).
detailed_answer: According to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, a person who commits an act while being of unsound mind is not considered to have committed an offence if they are incapable of knowing the nature of the act or that it is wrong (Section 22 Body, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023). Additionally, if an act is done in good faith for the benefit of a person of unsound mind, it is not an offence due to any harm it may cause (Section 27 Body, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023). However, this does not apply if the act involves the voluntary causing of grievous hurt unless it is for specific purposes such as preventing death or curing a grievous disease (Section 27(c), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023).
final_answer: A person of unsound mind is not liable for acts they commit if they cannot understand the nature of those acts (Section 22). Additionally, acts done in good faith for their benefit are not considered offences (Section 27).
